name: Assimilation to a pattern (ilḥāq)
definition: Adding a letter to a word so that it matches a longer pattern and is treated like it: three-letter verbs made to match the four-letter daḥraja.
body: Jalbaba, 'to put on a cloak', adds a second bāʾ to j-l-b; ḥawqala adds a wāw; bayṭara adds a yāʾ: each now conjugates exactly like daḥraja (yujalbibu like yudaḥriju), and is called mulḥaq bi-daḥraja. The added letter gives no new meaning, which is what separates ilḥāq from the augmented patterns, whose letters do. Al-ʿIzzī and Marāḥ al-arwāḥ list the patterns of ilḥāq after the four-letter verb.

examples.text: jalbaba, from j-l-b with a second bāʾ.
